evals.prompt: Grill me on this plan: I want to move our job queue from cron to a message broker next sprint.
evals.expected_output: Interviews one question at a time, each with a Q and a GUESS, and waits for the reaction before asking the next.
assertions: Asks exactly one question per turn in the Q / GUESS shape, with a falsifiable hypothesis
Waits for the user's reaction before asking the next question
Explores the codebase instead of asking anything git log or grep can answer
Does not stop until it can predict the user's reaction to the next three questions

evals.prompt: Stress-test my design for the export feature. I think we are aligned now, you can wrap up.
evals.expected_output: Runs the 95% predictive test, then restates Outcome, User, Why now, Success, Constraint and Out of scope and asks for an explicit yes.
assertions: Applies the predictive test (can predict reactions to the next 3 questions) rather than stopping on vibe
Restates with the fields Outcome, User, Why now, Success, Constraint, Out of scope
Asks for an explicit yes before moving on
Treats 'whatever you think is best' or 'sounds good' as non-convergence and follows up

evals.prompt: Rename the function parseCfg to parseConfig across the repo.
evals.expected_output: Unambiguous mechanical operation: do it directly, no interview.
assertions: Performs the rename without asking interview questions
Does not manufacture doubt when confidence is already at least 95 percent
